speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me when your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice a red, expanding "bull's-eye" rash on your skin during or after the camping trip? Have you observed any tick bites on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists and hands, combined with monoarticular arthritis and a recent trip to Minnesota, is highly suggestive of disseminated gonococcal infection. To confirm this, I need to test for the causative organism. REQUEST TEST: Gram stain and culture of joint fluid. REQUEST TEST: Nucleic acid amplification test for Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
